flashcard_questions.q: Which phrase does Lady Macbeth use for her husband’s gentleness in Act 1, Scene 5?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘Too full o’ th’ milk of human kindness.’
A mild or indirect expression used for something unpleasant or taboo.

flashcard_questions.q: Which euphemism does Lady Macbeth use instead of naming murder?
Which three-word command does Lady Macbeth give the spirits about her gender?
What does Lady Macbeth ask the spirits to put in place of her milk?
Which line instructs Macbeth to hide murderous intent behind a gentle face?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘Look like the innocent flower, but be the serpent under’t.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which biblical story does that serpent image allude to?
flashcard_questions.a: The Devil tempting Eve in the Garden of Eden.

flashcard_questions.q: What does transgressive mean when applied to a character?
flashcard_questions.a: They defy the accepted rules and expectations of their society.

flashcard_questions.q: Which phrase does Macbeth use for his only motive to kill Duncan?
Which line shows Macbeth deciding to abandon the murder plan?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘We will proceed no further in this business.’

flashcard_questions.q: How does Lady Macbeth attack Macbeth’s masculinity in Act 1, Scene 7?
flashcard_questions.a: ‘When you durst do it, then you were a man.’

flashcard_questions.q: Which shocking image does Lady Macbeth use to prove her own commitment?
flashcard_questions.a: Dashing out the brains of her smiling, nursing baby.

flashcard_questions.q: Which title does Macbeth give his wife that treats her as an equal?
Which label does Malcolm give Lady Macbeth at the end of the play?
How does Lady Macbeth’s language change by Act 5?
flashcard_questions.a: It breaks into fragmented prose instead of verse.

notes: 15 cards: 8 quotation-recall fronts, 2 quotation-to-effect (the serpent allusion, the infanticide image), 2 term-to-definition (euphemism, transgressive), 1 quotation-to-technique (the ‘unsex me’ imperative), 2 form/structure cards (the Act 5 shift to prose, ‘dearest partner of greatness’ as a marker of equality). ‘Soliloquy’, ‘imperatives’, ‘biblical allusion’ and ‘duplicity’ dropped as glossary restatements that would interfere with the quotation cards already testing them. All quotations verbatim from the lesson content.
